column1: # PX3 - known macOS Audio Unit hosts.
# SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH. The installer, the uninstaller and the tests all read
# this file; bundle identifiers are not written anywhere else.
# The plugin being protected is PX3Synth.component, an Audio Unit INSTRUMENT, so
# this lists applications that can load AU instruments and therefore could have
# the bundle open. It is deliberately NOT a list of "audio applications":
# matching on process names or audio-related keywords is what produced false
# positives, most notably `auval`, which macOS runs by itself after any Audio
#   local    - read from the application's own Info.plist on a machine we tested
# Identifiers are matched case-insensitively and by exact string. Several
# vendors ship version-specific identifiers, so more than one may be listed.
# Add new hosts here and nowhere else.
#       Validation tools. macOS launches `auval` on its own after an Audio Unit
#       is installed, so treating it as a host blocked the installer moments
#       after a successful install. This was the original false positive.
#   AudioComponentRegistrar, coreaudiod, audiomxd, and other CoreAudio daemons
#       System services. They never load a plugin into a user session.
#   Spotify, QuickTime Player, browsers, conferencing apps, media players
#       Play audio; cannot host an Audio Unit instrument.
#       Windows-only products. They have no macOS bundle identifier, so no
#       identifier is invented for them here.
